stories.headline: AWS publishes a complete multi-turn reinforcement-learning pipeline for agents
stories.summary: AWS shows a complete multi-turn reinforcement-learning pipeline for teaching GPT-OSS-20B to play Wordle on SageMaker AI. Its reported solve rate rose from 61% to 84% at default reasoning effort and from 15% to 69% at low effort, using outcome rewards, AgentCore execution and iterative rollout training.
stories.why_it_matters: You will learn how to frame an agent task, define outcome rewards, collect multi-turn rollouts and compare pretraining with post-training. The cost breakdown and failure modes help teams decide whether a bounded RL experiment is worth running.

source.title: Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning on Amazon SageMaker AI: A hands-on guide

read_evidence.scope: Reviewed the complete AWS technical guide, Wordle task environment, GPT-OSS-20B baseline and trained solve rates, AgentCore runtime, outcome-dominant reward design, training sequence, estimated costs, failure analysis and stated limitations.

stories.related_coverage: Adds an end-to-end, costed procedure for post-training a multi-turn agent and measuring task success.
stories.image_alt_intent: A multi-turn agent repeatedly solving Wordle inside a reinforcement-learning loop, with before-and-after solve-rate gauges and separate cost labels for training and execution.

stories.headline: IBM keeps interpretability hooks compatible with high-performance vLLM execution
stories.summary: IBM Research introduces vLLM-Hook, a model-internals access layer that preserves vLLM graph replay while supporting activation inspection and steering. In publisher-run experiments, the team reports up to 20× lower instrumentation overhead than its predecessor, with roughly 2% overhead on small models and 6% on a 70-billion-parameter model.
stories.why_it_matters: You will learn where interpretability tooling can distort production inference and how graph-aware hooks reduce that penalty. The reported overhead ranges also provide a practical benchmark for deciding whether observability experiments belong in a serving-path evaluation.

source.title: Toward fast AI interpretability and control

read_evidence.scope: Reviewed the complete IBM Research article, the Model Instrumentation Architecture plugin, graph-replay compatibility, activation inspection and steering workflow, comparative speed claims, 2% and 6% overhead reports, experimental setup and publisher-evidence limitations.

source.freshness_reason: Extended fallback is justified because IBM’s October 21 post provides the only reviewed graph-replay-compatible interpretability measurements, and no newer primary source covered the same serving-path decision.

stories.related_coverage: Extends model observability coverage with a serving-path implementation and explicit overhead measurements.
stories.image_alt_intent: A high-throughput inference engine retaining graph replay while transparent hooks inspect and steer internal activations, beside gauges showing reported overhead across small and 70-billion-parameter models.

stories.headline: Google Cloud splits Claude deployment between managed features and stricter platform control
stories.focus: Applied Generative AI for Knowledge Workers
stories.summary: Google Cloud now offers Claude through two deployment paths: an Anthropic-managed experience with early access to agents, skills and code execution, and a Google-managed path with Vertex AI controls such as CMEK and data residency. Google says the same frontier models and pricing apply, while processors, terms and feature timing differ.
stories.why_it_matters: You will learn how to compare processor roles, contract terms, regional controls and feature cadence before choosing a deployment path. That checklist helps procurement, security and operations teams avoid treating identical model names as identical governance choices.

source.title: Expanding Claude availability and deployment choice on Google Cloud

read_evidence.scope: Reviewed the complete Google Cloud announcement, Anthropic-managed and Google-managed deployment paths, processor roles, contract differences, day-zero managed features, Vertex controls, CMEK, data residency, pricing statement and availability caveats.

coverage_labels: Applied Generative AI for Knowledge Workers
stories.related_coverage: Gives workplace AI buyers a concrete comparison between feature velocity and Google-managed governance controls.
stories.image_alt_intent: Two deployment lanes for the same Claude models: one emphasizing early managed-agent features and another emphasizing Vertex controls, with a decision checklist for processor, terms, regions and feature cadence.

stories.headline: Uber takes ChatGPT Work from a 1,000-person pilot to more than 30,000 employees
stories.focus: Applied Generative AI for Knowledge Workers
stories.summary: Uber is rolling ChatGPT Work out to more than 30,000 employees after a 1,000-person pilot. The deployment connects workplace tools including Google Drive, Gmail, Calendar and Slack, and supports research, briefs, presentations and data work. Uber is also building an internal skills library and role-specific training, while measurable outcome data remains forthcoming.
stories.why_it_matters: You will learn how a large employer moved from pilot access to organization-wide enablement using connectors, reusable skills and training. The account also highlights the missing measurement layer, giving leaders a concrete agenda for adoption, governance and outcome tracking.

source.title: Uber brings ChatGPT Work to all employees with OpenAI

read_evidence.scope: Reviewed the complete OpenAI and Uber case study, pilot and rollout sizes, named workplace connectors, research and presentation workflows, internal skills library, role-specific training, stated future plans and absence of published outcome measurements.

coverage_labels: Applied Generative AI for Knowledge Workers
stories.related_coverage: Provides a large-scale knowledge-work rollout while distinguishing access and enablement from independently measured outcomes.
stories.image_alt_intent: A workplace rollout expanding from a 1,000-person pilot to more than 30,000 employees, with connected-tool icons, an internal skills library and a blank measurement panel awaiting outcome evidence.

stories.headline: Anthropic moves the Agent Skills standard into neutral Linux Foundation governance
stories.summary: Anthropic has donated the Agent Skills specification, reference SDKs and repositories to the Linux Foundation’s Agentic AI Foundation. A Skill is a folder built around a plain-language SKILL.md file, with optional templates and references. Anthropic says more than 70 platforms support the format, while neutral governance will address versioning, security and interoperability.
stories.why_it_matters: You will learn a noncoding method for turning one repeated office workflow into a reviewed Skill: document instructions and outputs, test normal and adverse cases, assign ownership and a review date, then approve a version before reuse.

source.title: Donating Agent Skills to the Agentic AI Foundation

read_evidence.scope: Reviewed the complete Anthropic announcement, donation scope, SKILL.md structure, optional scripts and references, stated support across more than 70 platforms, adoption claims, Linux Foundation governance role, versioning and security roadmap, and publisher-claim limitations.

stories.related_coverage: Updates reusable-Skills coverage with neutral governance and a portable, noncoding office-workflow procedure.
stories.image_alt_intent: A plain-language SKILL.md folder moving from one vendor into neutral foundation governance, with a seven-step office-workflow review path and badges for ownership, versioning and approval.
stories.agent_skills_evidence: Reusable noncoding procedure: choose one repeated office review workflow; describe its purpose, inputs, output standards and approved templates in plain-language SKILL.md instructions; test normal and adverse examples on two compatible assistants; compare results with the current process; correct failures; assign an owner, version and review date; then approve the bounded Skill before team reuse.

audience_fit.intended_user: An operations leader who maintains recurring review workflows, approved templates and quality standards in ordinary office tools.
audience_fit.practical_action: Choose one repeated review task and write plain-language instructions, required inputs, output standards and approved templates in a Skill folder.
audience_fit.review_action: Test normal and adverse examples on two compatible assistants, compare results with the current workflow and correct failures before approval.
audience_fit.usable_outcome: A versioned, owner-assigned and review-dated Skill approved for a bounded team pilot without requiring programming work.

stories.headline: TK Elevator puts an evidence-grounded mobile agent beside 25,000 service technicians
stories.summary: Microsoft and TK Elevator describe a mobile AI assistant for 25,000 service technicians maintaining 1.4 million units. Before a visit, it assembles tools, location details and likely issues from IoT data, manuals and notes. Afterward, a voice debrief gathers missing facts, while technicians retain responsibility for diagnosis and action.
stories.why_it_matters: You will learn how to structure a field-service workflow around pre-visit briefs, evidence retrieval, voice debriefs and human decision authority. The pattern helps operations leaders evaluate assistance that reduces search and documentation work without delegating safety-critical judgment.

source.title: Data and AI agents give a lift to TK Elevator service technicians

read_evidence.scope: Reviewed the complete Microsoft and TK Elevator feature, 25,000-technician and 1.4-million-unit scope, pre-visit brief, IoT and manual retrieval, mobile access, voice debrief, follow-up questions, human responsibility, vendor-case-study framing and limitations.

stories.related_coverage: Shows a noncoding frontline workflow in which an agent assembles evidence and documentation while technicians retain decision authority.
stories.image_alt_intent: A service technician using a phone beside an elevator, with an agent brief assembling tools, IoT signals, manuals and prior notes before a human-approved repair and voice debrief.

audience_fit.intended_user: A field-service operations leader who manages technician preparation, evidence access, debrief quality and human accountability.
audience_fit.practical_action: Select one recurring service visit and define the pre-visit facts, approved evidence sources, debrief questions and decisions reserved for technicians.
audience_fit.review_action: Compare agent briefs and voice debriefs with completed work orders, then record omissions, unsupported suggestions and technician corrections.
audience_fit.usable_outcome: A bounded field-service pilot with a source checklist, human decision boundary, debrief template and measurable documentation-quality review.

videos.summary: IBM Technology explains the inference path from tokenization through prefill and autoregressive decoding, then connects batching, GPU work and KV-cache reuse to latency, throughput and serving cost.
videos.why_it_matters: The concise lesson gives engineers a shared vocabulary for locating inference bottlenecks and choosing measurements before evaluating serving optimizations such as batching, cache management, quantization or parallelism.

Benchmark task-shaped requests rather than relying on one aggregate tokens-per-second number.
